findings.reason: the section must extend the shared renderer at query_builder.py:268 (so the one owner carries the negation for both families) or migrate the five path claims to `build_path_prefix_filter`, otherwise the design names a mechanism that does not cover half the sites it mandates.
findings.text: §24 places the exclusion negation on `build_path_prefix_filter` (:282), but the five path claims reach the prefix clause through `render_path_prefix_clause` directly, not through the builder — the census of clause entry points is: five path claims at imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:484, 540, 597, 715, 795 (each `render_path_prefix_clause("p", "root_filter")`), the scoped reset at imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:108, and the ten code sites plus the ingest worker that use `build_path_prefix_filter` (imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:132, 304, 399, 485, 580, 620, 644, 674, 707, 734 and imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:566) — so a `negated` flag on the builder alone leaves the path claims, which §24 explicitly requires to skip excluded rows, unable to express it

findings.reason: a single helper taking `(facility, alias)` and returning the clause plus its parameters would hide the policy behind one interface and remove the per-site drift the plan otherwise relies on a test to catch, which is the whole point of a deep module over a spread of shallow edits.
findings.text: §24 requires every path and code claim and every phase-liveness predicate to consult the facility's exclusion prefixes, which means each of the sites in the census above (plus `has_pending_work` at paths/parallel.py:197 and its `_has_pending_scan/expand/triage/enrich/score_work` helpers at :265-338, and the code has-work predicates at code/graph_ops.py:566-734) independently resolves `get_exclusion_config_for_facility(facility)` and composes the negated clause, spreading one policy across roughly fifteen call sites with nothing that makes a site fail if it forgets

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §24 threads the exclusion policy through ~15 claim and liveness sites, each re-resolving the facility's `ExclusionConfig`, instead of hiding the policy behind one interface that takes the facility id.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the shared prefix clause has two entry points and §24 names only one of them, so the mechanism it cites cannot reach the path claims the section also requires to honour the exclusion.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §24 adds no new public definition (it broadens an existing builder with a flag) and the landed §14 nodes retired surface (`seed_missing_roots`, `create_child_paths`) rather than adding any, so no live section enlarges an interface family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the live sections name existing owners and the code confirms each: `should_exclude`'s basename matching for `directories` (imas_codex/config/discovery_config.py:165), `build_path_prefix_filter` (imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:282), `GraphClient.create_nodes(create_only=...)` (imas_codex/graph/client.py:611), `ResetSpec.source_filter` (imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:45) and `seed_facility_roots` (imas_codex/discovery/paths/frontier.py:426); the plan extends these rather than rebuilding them.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §24's `negated` flag extends the existing prefix builder rather than adding a parallel wrapper, and says why (one builder keeps clause and binding together).
